newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mystery buyer wants big Burns stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mystery buyer wants big Burns stake - paper.

text.p: A mystery buyer has ordered broker Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to buy a stake of up to 10 percent of Australian based spices and yeast group Burns Philp & Co Ltd at A$2.50 a share, newspapers reported on Friday.

"We have been looking for about 10 percent of Burns, equal to 52.2 million shares, and we have an investor willing to pay A$2.50 apiece for the shares," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell director Robin Yandell was quoted as telling The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper.
The offer price is 47 cents above Burns' A$2.03 closing price on Thursday, indicative of a potential takeover bid.

"The client is not an international food company -- and we classify Goodman Fielder as an international food company -- it is an overseas-based individual that does not have any food assets at this stage," Yandel said.
There has been some recent speculation that Australian-based food group Goodman Fielder may make a takeover bid for Burns Philp.
The Sydney Morning Herald said Deutsche Morgan had acted for George Soros in the past.
The order was filled with sales from local and London-based institutions and the client was buying furhter shares, the broker said.

"It's early in the morning in New York and it may be that today I will have to negotiate with the sellers (institutions) to buy further scrip. At this stage we have got more than 10 percent," Yandel said.
The Australian newspaper said Deutsche Morgan was expected to bought the 53 million shares by the opening of trade on Friday.
The Australian Financial Review newspaper said some institutions believed the mystery buyer was a wealthy New Zealander, possibly Ron Brierley and his Guiness Peat Group Plc.
